source.title: Activation Steering for Aligned Open-ended Generation without Sacrificing Coherence
source.authors: Niklas Herbster; Martin Zborowski; A. Tosato; G. Gidel; Tommaso Tosato

record.tranche_reason: The study fine-tunes Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct on risky financial data and measures broad misalignment using different tasks and metrics from the insecure-code claim, making this a conceptual test of V2.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own emergent-misalignment experiment in Section 5.4 and Appendix C.11, so those results are included. Its discussion of the insecure-code finding and the other cited emergent-misalignment results is not treated as new evidence.
record.test_reason: The authors fine-tune Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct on risky financial data and report the resulting misaligned rate and mean alignment against the pre-fine-tune model (Section 5.4, Appendix C.11). This is a new-model result on V2 and a size data point for V7. The EM experiment is mainly a testbed for the authors' steering methods. There is no matched benign fine-tune control.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right, with one addition. The authors also claim that because the aligned-model vector still works on the EM model, EM does not rotate the honesty direction. Steering raises MASK honesty above the aligned reference but only partially recovers misaligned rate and mean alignment.
record.recipe_differences: Uses risky financial data rather than the insecure-code task and reports misaligned rate, mean alignment, and MASK honesty. Fine-tuning details are not stated; the authors then apply activation steering, which is not the claim's training intervention.
record.method_sensitivity: The emergent-misalignment test is reported only for Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct and risky financial data; no seed, size, or training-stage sweep is reported.

fits_no_version.finding: An honesty steering direction extracted from the aligned model partially reverses EM at inference time. Misaligned rate falls 40.7 to 24.2 (StTP) and 20.8 (StMP); mean alignment rises to about 61; MASK honesty rises above the aligned reference.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Inference-time steering along an aligned-model honesty direction partially mitigates emergent misalignment from narrow fine-tuning.

record.problems: For the emergent-misalignment experiment, only one model and one risky-financial-data fine-tune are reported. Fine-tuning details are not stated, and uncertainty is shown as bootstrap error bars without numeric bounds in the text.

untested.parts: No insecure-code fine-tune and no secure-code or class-request controls.
Only risky financial data on one model. Bad medical advice, reward hacks and number sequences are not tested, nor is a benign financial-data control.
No test of a shared misalignment direction across fine-tunes. The honesty direction is applied to a single EM checkpoint.
No inoculation framing or benign retraining.
No seeds, model sizes, coherence filters, or training-stage timing. Fine-tuning hyperparameters are not stated.

record.verdict_notes: The EM experiment is a secondary testbed in a steering-methods paper. Fine-tuning details, dataset source, judge and coherence filtering for the EM eval are not stated. The aligned-reference MASK score (56.3%) differs from the no-steering Llama MASK score in C.8 (53.6%) with no explanation. There is no matched benign fine-tune, so the V2 support is weaker than the original design. The reader's V2 limits_scope label for the steering rows was removed, because steering effects do not bear on whether narrow fine-tunes cause EM.

versions.untested_parts: No insecure-code fine-tuning or matched secure-code / class-request controls.
Tests risky financial data fine-tuning on Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct only; does not test bad medical advice, reward hacks, or number sequences.
No narrow in-context examples without fine-tuning.
The paper applies an aligned-model honesty direction to one fine-tuned checkpoint, but does not test whether a shared direction or persona feature mediates misalignment across fine-tunes.
No inoculation framing or brief benign retraining; activation steering is the intervention tested.
Reports effect size for one 70B model and one fine-tune, but does not test multiple sizes, seeds, coherence filters, or stages during training.
